summary: Kings Pass lookout, Coeur d'Alene NF: 40-foot pole L-4 tower built 1934, gone in the 1950s; footings, debris and an unidentified antenna remain.

facts.design: 40-foot pole L-4 tower on the west end of the ridge
facts.status_note: Both sites date its loss to the 1950s; footings, debris and a large microwave or antenna tower remain at the site.

access.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts says the access road is gated and visitors walk a few miles from the pass. It does not say the site is closed.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in: the gated road means a walk of a few miles from the pass.

events.note: 40-foot pole L-4 tower on the west end of the ridge; both sites date it to 1934
Henry Johnson listed as known staff, citing a Wallace Press-Times item of 06/07/1934
Abe Curley listed as known staff, citing a Wallace Press-Times item of 06/25/1935
Roy Norman listed as known staff; the Idaho list gives no citation for 1937

evidence.supports: 40-foot pole L-4 tower built in 1934 on the west end of the ridge; gone in the 1950s
evidence.quote: This 40' pole L-4 tower, built in 1934 on the west end of the ridge, was gone in the 1950's.

evidence.supports: Location 10 miles NNW of Wallace, Shoshone County
Built 1934 as L-4 on a pole tower
1934 known staff Henry Johnson, Wallace Press-Times citation
1935 known staff Abe Curley, Wallace Press-Times citation
Gated road; walk a few miles from the pass to where the lookout once stood
evidence.quote: it’s gated, so you’ll have to hoof it a few miles from the pass to where the lookout once stood out on the point

evidence.supports: Debris, old footings and number 9 wire remain
evidence.quote: Scattered debris, old footings, and some classic number 9 wire can still be found around the area.

evidence.supports: Large microwave or antenna system at the site, newer than the lookout era
evidence.quote: The most prominent is a large microwave tower or antenna system that looks far more modern than the 1950s era when the lookout was active.

evidence.supports: Origin of the antenna system not confirmed
evidence.quote: We haven’t been able to confirm whether this was ever a USFS electronic site or if it was used by another agency.

corrections.why: Firelookout.com says it was gone in the 1950's and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1950’s: Destroyed. Neither source gives 1950, so no destroyed event with a single year is recorded.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1950 destroyed year is not in either source; both give the 1950s (see corrections). The destroyed event is left out of events until the schema accepts a decade-only event. Staffing names come from the Idaho list, which cites Wallace Press-Times items that were not checked. The antenna system is unidentified; a reader comment on the Idaho page links it to the 1980s and is not used. No image URL was captured; firelookout.com credits a photo to Abe Turley but gives no file.
